title: You Trust Your AI Most on the Work You'll Check Least
summary: You check the AI hardest on work you could do yourself, and least on the work you handed off because you couldn't. That's backwards.
author: Jett Nguyen

title: Your AI Stops the Moment the Answer Looks Finished
summary: Your AI aims for a reply that looks done, not a task that is done. Those two only sometimes line up, and they come apart on exactly the boring jobs.
author: Jett Nguyen

title: You Asked for a Small Fix. Your AI Rewrote Everything Around It.
summary: You ask your AI to change one line. It changes the line, and quietly redoes four things you never mentioned. Here's why it can't tell the edit from the rewrite.
author: Jett Nguyen

title: Your AI Never Sounds Unsure. That's the Problem.
summary: Your AI uses the exact same calm, fluent voice whether it knows the answer or is guessing. Here's why, and what actually fixes it.
author: Jett Nguyen

title: The Best Reason to Run AI Locally Has Nothing to Do With Privacy
summary: Everyone sells local AI on privacy. That's the defensive reason. The real one is access: an agent that can reach your actual files and act.
author: Jett Nguyen

title: Your AI Agent Should Bother You More, Not Less
summary: The frictionless agent that never asks is a liability. The interruptions are the product, and on your own machine you get to draw the line.
author: Jett Nguyen

title: You're Not Giving the AI Instructions. You're Setting the Odds.
summary: Tiny prompt changes cause big swings because the model reads your words as the whole world and predicts from there. Here is the mechanism, and why owning the agent lets you keep the phrasing that works.
author: Jett Nguyen

title: Your AI Should Not Disappear When Your Computer Does
summary: When your computer breaks, your photos and files survive — but the context your AI has built about how you work usually doesn't. That accumulated history is becoming one of the most valuable parts of a personal AI, and it shouldn't be tied to one device. How Archie keeps your assistant's memory of you portable.
author: Jack Raney

title: The AI Model Isn't the Product Anymore. You Are.
summary: A year ago the only question about AI was which model is smartest. That's becoming the wrong question. As every company gets access to capable models, raw intelligence stops being the differentiator — the useful AI is the one that actually knows you. Why the next phase of AI is personal, not just powerful.
author: Jack Raney

title: How My Agent Caught What a Silent Outage Left Behind
summary: A minor complaint about a follow-up feature that never fired turned into a two-hour investigation: an expired credential nobody noticed, a hung daemon behind it, an appointment displayed two hours off, and a date parser that had never worked. Four bugs, all silent until someone kept asking.
author: Jack Raney

title: Everyone Is Either Scared of AI Agents or Ignoring Them. Both Are Wrong.
summary: AI agents are one of the most underrated shifts in how people work. Most people are either afraid of them or haven't thought about them at all. Here's what they're actually missing — and why the gap between "I use AI sometimes" and "I have an agent running my workflow" is going to matter a lot.
author: Jett Nguyen

title: My Business Agent Drafted a Fake Client Plan. Here's Exactly Why That Happened.
summary: The agent produced a professional email with a detailed action plan. It was also completely made up. Here's what was missing, why the model filled in the gaps confidently, and what building a reliable agent actually requires.
author: Jett Nguyen

title: My Workout App Didn't Know What I Should Lift. So I Built Something That Does.
summary: Every weekday, Jack's AI agent builds his workout from 60 days of training history, sleep, travel, and his golf schedule, then pushes it to his phone before he's out of bed. No mental math, no guessing what he lifted last week.
author: Jack Raney

title: I Got Socially Engineered by a Fake Google Call. My AI Agent Helped Me Stop What Came Next.
summary: A call from Google's real phone number talked Jack into handing over his Gmail account. Less than an hour later, his AI agent caught what he couldn't: hidden inbox filters, a planted passkey, and a backdoor built to survive a password reset.
author: Jack Raney
